fact: The Uganda Revenue Authority says ASYCUDA World is an online system used for processing all goods imported or exported, in which agents capture, validate and assess declarations and importers self-declare and pay taxes.

The Uganda Revenue Authority's Q&A column says importers lodge declarations in its customs system, where controlled HS codes need prior authorisation, while air-cargo manifest data entry is still manual.
The URA says it is in advanced stages of automating and integrating systems with airlines at Entebbe for electronic submission of cargo manifests before arrival.

The Uganda Revenue Authority says an automation process links EFRIS export invoices with ASYCUDA, and it trained clearing agents on 19 May 2025 ahead of export fiscalisation for exports outside the EAC.

A KRA officer writing in WCO News says Uganda Revenue Authority scans all cargo entering or leaving Uganda and matches it to customs declarations, sharing them through the EAC Single Customs Territory Centralized Platform since July 2024.

A KRA officer writing in WCO News says the EAC Single Customs Territory Centralized Platform, built for six partner states, has shared customs declarations and scanned-cargo images since July 2024, with Uganda sending over 8,000 images to Kenya.

Uganda's WTO notification G/TFA/N/UGA/4 of 12 June 2024 reports 22 of a target 45 agencies actively operational on the e-Single Window, with interfaces to commercial banks and online permits and certificates.
The Uganda Revenue Authority's UESW page says the single window is built on the ASYCUDA World platform and lists an upgrade of the customs ASYCUDA World system.
The Uganda Revenue Authority's UESW page says the Uganda Electronic Single Window has automated 22 of 30 border agencies, which can issue permits and certificates electronically.

TradeMark Africa reports that the customs systems of Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi are interconnected through the East African Community Single Customs Territory Centralised Platform, with scanner image sharing first implemented between Kenya and Uganda in 2024.
system: EAC Single Customs Territory Centralised Platform
